Run the complete evolution of Prakrti

Source: R/samkhya_evolution.R
samkhya_evolve.Rd

Carries the evolution from the unmanifest equilibrium through to the gross elements, following the branching derivation of Samkhya-Karika 22 and 25 rather than a single linear chain.

Usage

samkhya_evolve(
  guna_dominant = c("sattva", "rajas", "tamas"),
  delta = 0.1,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

guna_dominant

Which quality predominates when the equilibrium breaks. Passed to evolution_buddhi().

delta

Magnitude of the disturbance. Passed to evolution_buddhi().

verbose

Emit progress messages at each step. Default TRUE.

Value

A samkhya_state in which all twenty-three evolutes of Prakrti have manifested.

Details

The order in which the two branches from ahamkara are taken is immaterial, since they issue in parallel; this function takes the vaikrta branch first only because the karika enumerates the elevenfold set first. Taking the bhutadi branch first yields an identical final state, which the package test suite asserts.

References

Isvarakrsna. Samkhyakarika, verses 22, 25.

See also

init_prakriti() and the individual evolution functions for the step-by-step form, get_kaivalya() for what follows completion, plot.samkhya_state(), create_samkhya_flowchart().

Examples

state <- samkhya_evolve(verbose = FALSE)
state
#> <samkhya_state>
#> Stage: Mahabhutas (the specific)
#> Gunas: sattva = 0.433, rajas = 0.283, tamas = 0.283 (sum = 1.000)
#> Evolutes manifest: 23 of 23
#> Cognitive situation: Visesa (the specific): the gross world stands manifest
#> Viveka in buddhi: Not attained
#> Prakrti acting for this Purusha: Yes
#> Purusha: Witness, neutral, non-agent; neither bound nor released (SK 19, 62)

# All twenty-three evolutes of Prakrti are present.
summary(state)$n_manifest
#> [1] 23
